history.dynasty: Rashtrakuta (mid-10th century vimana) and Western Chalukya (consecration ~987 AD by Duggimayya under Tailapa II / Ahava Malla); later modifications under Chalukyas and Hoysalas
history.period: Mid-10th century to 987 AD; ASI-protected monument of national importance
history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple at Bagali (ancient Balgali) whose construction spans the Rashtrakuta mid-10th century and the Western Chalukya consecration of 987 AD by Duggimayya under King Tailapa II (Ahava Malla). Adam Hardy classifies it as a late Rashtrakuta vimana with erotic carvings (hence 'Karnataka's Khajuraho') plus a closed mantapa fronted by a Later Chalukya open mantapa, in soapstone. The trikuta-style complex enshrines the Kalleshwara linga with Narasimha and Surya in the other cells; 36 old Kannada inscriptions (10th-11th centuries) were found here. Note: one travel source claims Harpanahalli taluk has moved to Ballari district - UNVERIFIED; ASI and encyclopaedic sources place it in Davangere district.

name: Bagali Kalleshwara Temple
town_description: CSV town 'Davangere' corrected: the temple is at Bagali (ancient Balgali/Baguli) village in Harpanahalli taluk, Davangere district, about 9 km from Harpanahalli and ~52 km from Davangere. It was an important medieval agrahara and briefly a capital under Hoysala king Ballala II. The village is famous for the Kalleshwara temple complex with nearby Panchalinga shrines and kalyanis; coordinates are from the published temple record (14.84389N, 75.98278E).

travel.road: 9 km from Harpanahalli; ~52 km by road from Davangere
